claim: An organization instance of IAM Identity Center is deployed in the AWS Organizations management account and is the only instance type that can manage access to AWS accounts; AWS recommends it for all production use of applications.
question: Which IAM Identity Center instance type can manage access to AWS accounts, and where is it deployed?

values.display: deployed in the AWS Organizations management account
manage access to AWS accounts
recommended for all production use of applications

qualifiers.scope: organization instance of IAM Identity Center

evidence.quote: It's the only instance that enables you to manage access to AWS accounts and it is recommended for all production use of applications.
An organization instance is deployed in the AWS Organizations management account and gives you a single point from which to manage user access across AWS.

claim: An account instance of IAM Identity Center is bound to a single AWS account and is visible only within that account and the Region where it is enabled; AWS says to use account instances only for isolated deployments of select AWS managed applications.
question: What is an account instance of IAM Identity Center limited to, and when should it be used?

values.display: bound to a single AWS account
visible only within the AWS account
isolated deployments of select AWS managed applications

qualifiers.scope: account instance of IAM Identity Center

evidence.quote: An instance of IAM Identity Center that is bound to a single AWS account, and that is visible only within the AWS account and AWS Region in which it is enabled.
Use account instances of IAM Identity Center only to support isolated deployments of select AWS managed applications.

claim: AWS Organizations is recommended but not required for IAM Identity Center; enabling IAM Identity Center with AWS Organizations creates an organization instance.
question: Does IAM Identity Center require AWS Organizations, and what does enabling it with Organizations create?

values.display: recommended, but not required
which creates an organization instance of IAM Identity Center

evidence.quote: AWS Organizations is recommended, but not required, for use with IAM Identity Center.
We recommend that you enable IAM Identity Center with AWS Organizations, which creates an organization instance of IAM Identity Center.

claim: To add IAM Identity Center to an existing organization, all features of AWS Organizations must be enabled.
question: Which AWS Organizations feature set must be enabled to add IAM Identity Center to an organization?

values.display: all AWS Organizations features are enabled

qualifiers.scope: an existing organization in AWS Organizations
qualifiers.condition: adding IAM Identity Center to the organization

evidence.quote: If you've already set up AWS Organizations and are going to add IAM Identity Center to your organization, make sure that all AWS Organizations features are enabled.

claim: An organization instance of IAM Identity Center is enabled by signing in to the AWS Organizations management account; with administrative credentials from a member account you can enable an account instance.
question: From which account is an organization instance of IAM Identity Center enabled, and what can a member account enable?

values.display: your AWS Organizations management account
you can enable an account instance

qualifiers.scope: enabling an IAM Identity Center instance

evidence.quote: To enable an organization instance of IAM Identity Center, you must sign in to the AWS Management Console by signing in to your AWS Organizations management account as a user that has administrative credentials or as the root user (not recommended unless no other administrative users exist).
When signed in with administrative credentials from an AWS Organizations member account, you can enable an account instance of IAM Identity Center.

claim: All data configured in IAM Identity Center, including directory configurations, permission sets, application instances and user assignments, is stored in the Region where IAM Identity Center was enabled.
question: Where does IAM Identity Center store its configuration data?

values.display: stored in the Region where you enabled it
directory configurations, permission sets, application instances

evidence.quote: When you enable IAM Identity Center, all the data that you configure in IAM Identity Center is stored in the Region where you enabled it. This data includes directory configurations, permission sets, application instances, and user assignments to AWS account applications.

claim: When an IAM Identity Center instance is replicated to additional Regions, IAM Identity Center automatically replicates users, groups, permission sets and their assignments, and other metadata and configuration to those Regions.
question: What does IAM Identity Center copy when the instance is replicated to additional Regions?

values.display: automatically replicates users, groups, permission sets
permission sets and their assignments

qualifiers.scope: organization instance replicated to additional Regions
qualifiers.condition: the instance is replicated to additional Regions

evidence.quote: If you replicate your IAM Identity Center instance to additional Regions, IAM Identity Center automatically replicates users, groups, permission sets and their assignments, and other metadata and configuration to those Regions.

note: d060. Multi-Region replication is a recent feature; its GA date belongs to the numbers+changes lens (check against the 2026-07-15 examinable cut-off).

claim: A permission set is a template, created and maintained by the administrator, that defines a collection of one or more IAM policies and is used to assign AWS account access to users and groups.
question: What is a permission set in IAM Identity Center?

values.display: a template that you create and maintain
simplify the assignment of AWS account access

evidence.quote: A permission set is a template that you create and maintain that defines a collection of one or more [IAM policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html). Permission sets simplify the assignment of AWS account access for users and groups in your organization.

claim: A permission set can hold AWS managed policies, customer managed policies, inline policies and AWS managed policies for job functions, and can use an AWS managed policy or a customer managed policy as a permissions boundary.
question: Which policy types can a permission set contain, and can it have a permissions boundary?

values.display: AWS managed policy or a customer managed policy
to your permission sets

evidence.quote: You can add [AWS managed policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_managed-vs-inline.html#aws-managed-policies), [customer managed policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_managed-vs-inline.html#customer-managed-policies), [inline policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_managed-vs-inline.html#inline-policies), and [AWS managed policies for job functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html) to your permission sets. You can also assign an AWS managed policy or a customer managed policy as a [permissions boundary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html).

claim: When a permission set is assigned, IAM Identity Center creates IAM Identity Center-controlled IAM roles in each account and attaches the permission set's policies; when the permission set is modified, IAM Identity Center updates the corresponding IAM policies and roles.
question: What happens in the member accounts when a permission set is assigned and later modified?

values.display: attaches the policies specified in the permission set
corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly

qualifiers.scope: accounts where the permission set is assigned

evidence.quote: When you assign a permission set, IAM Identity Center creates corresponding IAM Identity Center-controlled IAM roles in each account, and attaches the policies specified in the permission set to those roles.
As you modify the permission set, IAM Identity Center ensures that the corresponding IAM policies and roles are updated accordingly.

claim: IAM roles whose names begin with AWSReservedSSO_ are the roles IAM Identity Center created in the account when a permission set was assigned to it.
question: What are the IAM roles named AWSReservedSSO_ in an account?

values.display: came from assigning a permission set
the IAM Identity Center service has created

qualifiers.scope: member accounts with permission set assignments

evidence.quote: These are the roles which the IAM Identity Center service has created in the account, and they came from assigning a permission set to the account.
If you are reviewing IAM roles in an account that is already using IAM Identity Center, you might notice role names beginning with “AWSReservedSSO\_”.

claim: When IAM Identity Center is enabled for the first time, it is automatically configured with the Identity Center directory as the default identity source unless a different identity source is chosen.
question: What is the default identity source of a new IAM Identity Center instance?

values.display: Identity Center directory as your default identity source

qualifiers.condition: unless a different identity source is chosen

evidence.quote: When you enable IAM Identity Center for the first time, it is automatically configured with an Identity Center directory as your default identity source unless you choose a different identity source.
